references.text: The expression 'to fill the hand' (וַיְמַלֵּא אֶת־יַד) is the technical Hebrew term for ordaining a priest to service, as described in the consecration of Aaron and his sons.
The consecration of Aaron and his sons to the priesthood uses the same expression 'to fill the hand,' indicating official ordination to priestly service.
Moses urges the Levites to consecrate themselves ('fill their hands') to the Lord, showing the same terminology for consecration to holy service.
Micah had previously ordained one of his own sons as a priest before the Levite arrived, demonstrating his unauthorized religious practice.
The young Levite later confirms to the Danites that Micah had hired him as his priest.
This Levite is later identified as Jonathan, son of Gershom, Moses' grandson, who served as priest for the tribe of Dan.
The lawful consecration of priests was to last seven days at the entrance of the tabernacle, in contrast to Micah's private ordination.
